title: Cheese and Vegetable Pizza, Thin Crust (Frozen)

content.title: About
content.content: Thin frozen cheese and vegetable pizza is a convenient option for a quick lunch or dinner. The crust is thin and crispy, topped with tomato sauce, plant-based cheese, and a mix of vegetables such as bell pepper, onion, mushrooms, and olives. The pizza is designed for baking in a conventional oven or heating in a microwave.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crust requires a shorter baking time than traditional thick crust.
Frozen pizzas often use pre‑cooked vegetables to preserve flavor and texture.
The cheese blend typically includes mozzarella and other melt‑friendly cheeses for even melting.
In many countries, added herbs like oregano or basil are mixed directly into the dough.
Rapid freezing technology retains most of the vitamins and minerals in the vegetables.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The cheese provides both dairy and plant protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and fiber, supporting overall health.

items.title: Lower fat content with moderate consumption
items.content: Thin crust contains fewer calories than thick crust, and a moderate amount of cheese helps control saturated fat intake.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables aids regular bowel movements.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Tomatoes and vegetables are rich in lycopene and other antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made pizzas often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Some commercial doughs may include partially hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Frozen pizzas can be calorie‑dense; it is important to follow the recommended serving size.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (390 °F). Place the pizza on a rack or baking sheet and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the crust is golden and the cheese is fully melted. Optionally add fresh herbs before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the pizza in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing, cook immediately. Do not keep thawed pizza at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
